abstract: Mixed reality could bring interfaces into the user's world, yet the responses of intelligent agents in MR today remain speech, flat windows, or visualizations built for a single scenario. We present ModOS, a system that synthesis on-demand spatial interfaces from MODs: units of knowledge and representation that people add to their environment ahead of time. ModOS organizes memory around physical environments, and for each request determines and composes primitive representations anchored in the physical world, so that responses fit the moment and behave as the user expects. We derived basic MODs from everyday demands and refined them in a formative study. We conducted an exploratory study to understand how people use ModOS on Apple Vision Pro in a shared lab space, and a usability study of the tailoring tool [Findings TBD.]
